entities.summary: Bernard de Languissel was a French Catholic cardinal and archbishop who played a pivotal role in the politics of Western Europe during the late 13th century. Born in France, he rose through the ranks of the Catholic Church, becoming Archbishop of Reims in 1284, a position he held until his death in 1291. De Languissel was a key figure in the papal conclave that elected Pope Nicholas IV in 1288, a papacy that would have far-reaching consequences for the Catholic Church and Western Europe. He was also a close advisor to King Philip IV of France, who relied heavily on de Languissel's counsel in matters of state. Through his influence, de Languissel helped to secure the king's interests in the region and played a role in shaping the politics of Western Europe. De Languissel's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as he helped to establish the Catholic Church as a dominant force in Western Europe, paving the way for the Church's continued influence in the centuries to come. His impact can be seen in the many institutions and structures he helped to establish, including the University of Reims, which would become a center of learning and culture in the region. In the end, de Languissel's death in 1291 marked the end of an era, but his legacy continued to shape the course of Western European history for centuries to come.
